content.content:
them, against upstream with fwtest's 0001 and 0002.

| fwtest | App | What | Kind | fwtest | App |
|--------|-----|------|------|--------|-----|
| 0001 | none | The workspace manifest lists only the three vendored crates | build | yes | not needed: only for fwtest's three-crate copy |
| 0002 | B | A write to the LCD's SPI port's control register replaces it, so its interrupt enable can be cleared (SR-3) | bug fix | yes (0.2.0) | yes (its base) |
| 0003 | none | The block moves with a register base run in all eight modes (SR-7) | bug fix | yes (0.3.0) | no: to apply (harness/upstream/fm1-emu-block-moves.md) |
| 0004 | 0003 (A) | A dual-issue pair's head among the 4-byte ALU forms with no table class holds its result until after the pair | bug fix | yes (0.4.0) | yes |
| 0005 | none | The rotate right by a register runs, as a pair's head too | gap | yes (0.4.0) | no: to apply (harness/upstream/fm1-emu-undecoded-forms.md) |
| 0006 | none | The 4-byte push and pop of any register list run, not only lists from r0 | gap | yes (0.4.0) | no: to apply (same note) |
| 0007 | 0004 (C) | Peripheral addresses looked up before the memories | speed only | yes (0.4.0) | yes |
| 0008 | 0005 (D) | Code blocks in RAM found current by a count of writes to code, on every build | speed only | yes (0.4.0) | yes |
| 0009 | none | The MIDI output: the UART's transmit side sends bytes at the wire's pace and keeps them with their times, and its pending flag rises when the last has gone (it used to finish at once and send nothing) | model | yes (0.5.0) | no: to apply, with the bytes sent to CoreMIDI (harness/upstream/fm1-emu-midi-out.md) |
| none | 0006 (E) | Boot a raw image | the app's loader | no: fwtest has its own (in `harness/`, docs/HARNESS.md "The raw image") | yes |
| none | not a patch | Two pattern guards rewritten so the crates build on an older Rust | build | no: fwtest builds on Rust 1.99 | yes |

fwtest 0004, 0007 and 0008 are the app's 0003, 0004 and 0005 as they
stand: their added and removed lines are byte for byte the app's, only the
line offsets refreshed for fwtest's 0003. Once the app applies fwtest's
0003, 0005 and 0006, the two are the same source but for the app's
raw-image loader and its Rust 1.94 rewrite (which, its notes say, changes
nothing that decodes). That was checked on the app's patches as the owner
dropped them, not on its branch, which this side doesn't open: on upstream
with them, fwtest's three apply with line offsets only, the crates' own
tests pass, and the core crate is then byte for byte fwtest's. fwtest's
three need nothing newer than the Rust the app builds with.

## How each was checked

- **0004 (the pair heads).** From the vendor toolchain (PROVENANCE P-40):
  its disassembler prints the second twin of each of these forms (byte 1
  `f0` / `f1`) as a pair's head, and the compiler's own code for our
  firmware relies on a pair's second half seeing the registers as they
  were before the head. fwtest's harness test runs one word of every
  family, plain and as a pair's head, and fails without the patch. The
  app's own test comes with it.
- **0005 and 0006 (the two gaps SR-7 found).** Encodings from the vendor
  assembler and disassembler; the rotate's behaviour from the compiler's
  rotate idioms, including one built with the firmware's flags in a test
  image; the lists' from the lists from r0 the compiler emits. Each has a
  harness test that fails without it (docs/HARNESS.md, "Instructions").
- **0007 and 0008 (speed only).** Taken because a test shows they change
  no behaviour. The app's test for 0007 compares the new address lookup
  with the old one at every address up to the end of the memories and a
  sweep above. For 0008 every way RAM can be written was checked to count
  as a write to code, and a harness test runs RAM code changed by stores,
  with and without the patch. Then the firmware's suite (at `cdfd067`), the
  spec experiments and the harness's own suite were run on fwtest built
  with and without 0007 and 0008: all 284 output files are byte for byte
  the same.
- **0009 (the MIDI output, session midi-in-out).** The transmit side's
  registers from the SDK's register map and FM-1-RE's MIDI document; its
  timing from the MIDI wire format. A harness test and a suite case run a
  DMA, a single byte and one queued behind a transfer, with the UART off
  and on, and check every byte's time, the pending interrupt and the
  decoded messages. Without the patch there is nothing to capture, and
  the same image's interrupt record shows the difference: on 0.4.0 its
  handler ran twice, at once on each transfer (0 and 4.0 ms; a single
  byte raised nothing), on 0.5.0 three times, as each transfer's last
  byte ended (1.600, 3.320 and 5.281 ms); the suite case's golden file
  holds that record. The spec experiment E-21 does the same against the
  checkout's fwtest (C-SPEC-EXPERIMENTS). The
  input side and every other output are unchanged: the harness suite and
  the spec experiments match their earlier golden files, and the firmware
  suite (at `1537391`) gives the same 176 files as on 0.4.0 but for the
  version each `result.json` records and its new `midi_out_bytes_dropped`
  (0).
- **The firmware.** The same comparison between fwtest 0.3.0's emulator
  and 0.4.0's (0004 to 0008): no output of the three suites changed.

## Keeping them together

A patch that changes what the emulator does goes into both: in fwtest as a
numbered patch with a harness test that fails without it, in the app from
the note in `harness/upstream/`; this table gets a row. A speed-only patch
goes into fwtest only with a test that shows it changes nothing. When the
pinned upstream commit has a fix, both drop the patch.

  0008 takes that fix unchanged, the test only. Each run now enters the

  and not with it off, and ran again after the store. On an Apple silicon
  Mac the fixed test passes; with the count of writes to code switched
  off it fails, and its JIT half fails on its own. The old test, by the
  same count, ran no compiled code in either half. The patch's code is
  unchanged, so fwtest stays at 0.5.0 and no new image is pinned. Not run
  on an x86-64 host: fwtest's CI runs the harness's tests, not the
  crates'.
'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

## 16. MIDI input (SR-8)

### HW-67: The FM-1's MIDI inputs, and the one fwtest feeds
- Fact: The FM-1 takes MIDI in three ways, all active at once: a 3.5 mm
  MIDI IN jack carrying serial MIDI at 31 250 baud, USB MIDI (the FM-1 is a
  class-compliant USB device with a MIDI and an audio interface), and MIDI
  over Bluetooth LE. Its manual lists no MIDI OUT jack. On the chip, the
  jack's serial MIDI is received by UART1 (`JL_UART1`, HW-68), through its
  receive DMA. fwtest models only the jack:
  a script's `midi` event (HARNESS, "Input scripts") delivers its bytes to
  UART1's receiver, and fwtest has no USB or Bluetooth MIDI. Which pin the
  jack reaches, and how the TRS socket is wired (type A or B), the sources
  don't say (Q-12).
- Sources: MAN (the FM-1's manual, English part, p. 10, "MIDI
  Connectivity": the three interfaces, the jack's 31 250 baud; "What the
  FM-1 sends via MIDI"); RE `docs/io/05-midi.md` §1 and §2 (the three
  transports; UART MIDI on the UART at `0x00012100`, received by DMA),
  `docs/io/06-usb.md` §1 (a USB composite device, audio and MIDI),
  `docs/reversing/01-hardware-map.md` (MIDI I/O: USB and UART MIDI); SDK
  `WL82.h` lines 569-591 (UART1's base); E-19 (fwtest's `midi` bytes reach
  UART1's ring).
- Standing: confirmed (MAN, RE, SDK, E-19)
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

### HW-68: The UARTs' registers, sources, pins and clocks
- Fact: The chip has three UARTs, `JL_UART0`, `JL_UART1` and `JL_UART2`,
  at `0x00012000`, `0x00012100` and `0x00012200`. Each has the words, from
  its base: `CON0` +0x00, `CON1` +0x04, `BAUD` +0x08, `BUF` +0x0C, `OTCNT`
  +0x10, `TXADR` +0x14, `TXCNT` +0x18, `RXSADR` +0x1C, `RXEADR` +0x20,
  `RXCNT` +0x24, `HRXCNT` +0x28. `CON0`, `CON1`, `BAUD`, `TXCNT` and
  `HRXCNT` are 16 bits and `BUF` 8 bits, each in the low part of its word;
  `BAUD` and `TXCNT` are write-only and `HRXCNT` read-only. Their interrupt
  sources are 19, 20 and 21. A UART's transmit and receive pins are either
  one of its fixed pin pairs, given as transmit then receive (UART1: PH6 and
  PH7, PC3 and PC4, PB3 and PB4, or the USB pins), or any pin, through an
  output and an input channel of the port map (`JL_IOMAP`). The UART clock
  is the low-speed bus clock, the crystal oscillator or the PLL's 48 MHz
  (`CLK_CON1` bits 10-11, HW-53). The SDK's driver receives into a circular
  buffer by DMA, with an interrupt after a given number of bytes and an
  idle timeout counted in clocks, and each of the transmit, receive and
  timeout interrupts can be left off. The SDK gives no bit meanings for
  `CON0`, `CON1` or `BAUD` (its UART driver is a prebuilt library).
- Sources: SDK `WL82.h` lines 12-16 (the bases, `map_adr`) and 569-591
  (`JL_UART_TypeDef`, the three bases); SDK
  `include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/hwi.h` lines 59-61 (sources 19 to 21);
  SDK `include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/uart.h` (three UARTs, the pin pairs,
  the input and output channels); SDK `include_lib/driver/device/uart.h`
  (the clock choices, the circular buffer, the byte count and idle timeout,
  the interrupts that can be left off).
- Standing: confirmed (SDK)
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

### HW-69: UART1's receive flags, their acknowledge and the count latch
- Fact: In UART1's `CON0`, read: bit 14 is set when the receive DMA has
  taken the set number of bytes (receive pending), bit 11 when the line has
  been idle for the set time after a byte (timeout pending). Written as 1:
  bit 12 clears the receive pending, bit 10 the timeout pending, bit 13 the
  transmit pending; bit 7 latches into `HRXCNT` how many bytes the receive
  DMA has written since the previous latch, and `HRXCNT` keeps that count
  until the next latch. FM-1's own firmware receives MIDI from the jack
  this way, by DMA, on source 20.
- Sources: RE `docs/io/05-midi.md` §2.1 (the UART's flags at `0x00012100`:
  `0x4000` receive pending, `0x800` timeout; acknowledged with `0x80`,
  `0x1000`, `0x400`, `0x2000`; the count at `0x00012128` read in the
  handler); E-19 (the same bits in fwtest).
- Standing: confirmed (RE, E-19)
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

### HW-70: UART1's receive set-up bits, the ring, the count and the timeout
- Fact: In UART1's `CON0`: bit 0 turns the UART on; bit 2 enables the
  transmit interrupt, bit 3 the receive interrupt (bit 14, HW-69), bit 5
  the timeout interrupt (bit 11); bit 6 turns the receive DMA on. The DMA
  writes each byte at the next address of the ring from `RXSADR` up to,
  not including, `RXEADR`, and wraps to `RXSADR`; writing `RXSADR` starts
  it again at the ring's start. `RXCNT` is the number of bytes since the
  last latch that sets the receive pending (0: never). `OTCNT` is the idle
  time, in UART clocks (48 MHz from the PLL), after a byte that sets the
  timeout pending. The sources give no receive by `BUF` a byte at a time,
  no error flags (framing, overrun) and no `BAUD` formula (Q-12).
- Sources: the emulator model; SDK `include_lib/driver/device/uart.h`
  (that the receive is a DMA ring with a byte count and an idle timeout,
  not the bits); E-19, E-20 (fwtest behaves so).
- Standing: emulator-only
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

  jack's serial MIDI is received by UART1 (`JL_UART1`, HW-68), through its
  receive DMA. fwtest models only the jack:
  a script's `midi` event (HARNESS, "Input scripts") delivers its bytes to
  UART1's receiver, and fwtest has no USB or Bluetooth MIDI. Which pin the
  jack reaches, and how the TRS socket is wired (type A or B), the sources
  don't say (Q-12).
- Sources: MAN (the FM-1's manual, English part, p. 10, "MIDI
  Connectivity": the three interfaces, the jack's 31 250 baud; "What the
  FM-1 sends via MIDI"); RE `docs/io/05-midi.md` §1 and §2 (the three
  transports; UART MIDI on the UART at `0x00012100`, received by DMA),
  `docs/io/06-usb.md` §1 (a USB composite device, audio and MIDI),
  `docs/reversing/01-hardware-map.md` (MIDI I/O: USB and UART MIDI); SDK
  `WL82.h` lines 569-591 (UART1's base); E-19 (fwtest's `midi` bytes reach
  UART1's ring).
- Standing: confirmed (MAN, RE, SDK, E-19)
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

### HW-68: The UARTs' registers, sources, pins and clocks
- Fact: The chip has three UARTs, `JL_UART0`, `JL_UART1` and `JL_UART2`,
  at `0x00012000`, `0x00012100` and `0x00012200`. Each has the words, from
  its base: `CON0` +0x00, `CON1` +0x04, `BAUD` +0x08, `BUF` +0x0C, `OTCNT`
  +0x10, `TXADR` +0x14, `TXCNT` +0x18, `RXSADR` +0x1C, `RXEADR` +0x20,
  `RXCNT` +0x24, `HRXCNT` +0x28. `CON0`, `CON1`, `BAUD`, `TXCNT` and
  `HRXCNT` are 16 bits and `BUF` 8 bits, each in the low part of its word;
  `BAUD` and `TXCNT` are write-only and `HRXCNT` read-only. Their interrupt
  sources are 19, 20 and 21. A UART's transmit and receive pins are either
  one of its fixed pin pairs, given as transmit then receive (UART1: PH6 and
  PH7, PC3 and PC4, PB3 and PB4, or the USB pins), or any pin, through an
  output and an input channel of the port map (`JL_IOMAP`). The UART clock
  is the low-speed bus clock, the crystal oscillator or the PLL's 48 MHz
  (`CLK_CON1` bits 10-11, HW-53). The SDK's driver receives into a circular
  buffer by DMA, with an interrupt after a given number of bytes and an
  idle timeout counted in clocks, and each of the transmit, receive and
  timeout interrupts can be left off. The SDK gives no bit meanings for
  `CON0`, `CON1` or `BAUD` (its UART driver is a prebuilt library).
- Sources: SDK `WL82.h` lines 12-16 (the bases, `map_adr`) and 569-591
  (`JL_UART_TypeDef`, the three bases); SDK
  `include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/hwi.h` lines 59-61 (sources 19 to 21);
  SDK `include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/uart.h` (three UARTs, the pin pairs,
  the input and output channels); SDK `include_lib/driver/device/uart.h`
  (the clock choices, the circular buffer, the byte count and idle timeout,
  the interrupts that can be left off).
- Standing: confirmed (SDK)
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

### HW-69: UART1's receive flags, their acknowledge and the count latch
- Fact: In UART1's `CON0`, read: bit 14 is set when the receive DMA has
  taken the set number of bytes (receive pending), bit 11 when the line has
  been idle for the set time after a byte (timeout pending). Written as 1:
  bit 12 clears the receive pending, bit 10 the timeout pending, bit 13 the
  transmit pending; bit 7 latches into `HRXCNT` how many bytes the receive
  DMA has written since the previous latch, and `HRXCNT` keeps that count
  until the next latch. FM-1's own firmware receives MIDI from the jack
  this way, by DMA, on source 20.
- Sources: RE `docs/io/05-midi.md` §2.1 (the UART's flags at `0x00012100`:
  `0x4000` receive pending, `0x800` timeout; acknowledged with `0x80`,
  `0x1000`, `0x400`, `0x2000`; the count at `0x00012128` read in the
  handler); E-19 (the same bits in fwtest).
- Standing: confirmed (RE, E-19)
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

### HW-70: UART1's receive set-up bits, the ring, the count and the timeout
- Fact: In UART1's `CON0`: bit 0 turns the UART on; bit 2 enables the
  transmit interrupt, bit 3 the receive interrupt (bit 14, HW-69), bit 5
  the timeout interrupt (bit 11); bit 6 turns the receive DMA on. The DMA
  writes each byte at the next address of the ring from `RXSADR` up to,
  not including, `RXEADR`, and wraps to `RXSADR`; writing `RXSADR` starts
  it again at the ring's start. `RXCNT` is the number of bytes since the
  last latch that sets the receive pending (0: never). `OTCNT` is the idle
  time, in UART clocks (48 MHz from the PLL), after a byte that sets the
  timeout pending. The sources give no receive by `BUF` a byte at a time,
  no error flags (framing, overrun) and no `BAUD` formula (Q-12).
- Sources: the emulator model; SDK `include_lib/driver/device/uart.h`
  (that the receive is a DMA ring with a byte count and an idle timeout,
  not the bits); E-19, E-20 (fwtest behaves so).
- Standing: emulator-only
- Needed by: M6a (SR-8)

### HW-53: The clock registers
- Fact: `JL_CLOCK` is at `0x00010000`: `PWR_CON` +0, `SYS_DIV` +8,
  `CLK_CON0` +12, `CLK_CON1` +16, `CLK_CON2` +20, `CLK_CON3` +24. In
  `CLK_CON0`: bit 0 turns the RC oscillator on and bit 1 picks its rate
  (0: 250 kHz, 1: 16 MHz); bits 4-5 pick the oscillator input (0: the
  crystal oscillator, the SDK's "BT OSC"; 2: the RTC's low-frequency
  oscillator; 3: a pad); bits 6-8 pick the main (system) clock source:
  0 the RC oscillator, 4 the crystal oscillator, 6 the RTC's low-frequency
  oscillator, 7 the PLL. In `CLK_CON1`: bits 2-3 the DAC clock (0: PLL
  24 MHz, 1: oscillator, 2: low-speed bus clock, 3: off); bits 10-11 the
  UART clock (0: oscillator, 1: PLL 48 MHz, 2: low-speed bus clock, 3:
  off). The SDK's definitions of the PLL's control fields and of `SYS_DIV`'s
  fields are switched off in its header (they may belong to another chip),
  so they are not given here (Q-2). In fwtest none of these registers has

### HW-72: The SMK-37's MIDI OUT, and the FM-1's
- Fact: M-VAVE's SMK-37 Pro, the FM-1's sibling keyboard, has a 3.5 mm
  MIDI OUT jack on its rear panel. It reaches an external device's MIDI IN
  through a 3.5 mm-to-MIDI adapter, so it carries serial MIDI: the MIDI 1.0
  wire format, a current loop at 31 250 baud, each byte one start bit,
  eight data bits from the least significant, one stop bit, no parity. It
  also sends MIDI over USB (a class-compliant device) and Bluetooth LE. So
  its MIDI OUT is a UART's transmit side, not USB or Bluetooth. The FM-1
  has no MIDI OUT jack (HW-67). Which UART and pin drive the SMK-37's jack,
  and how its TRS socket is wired (type A or B), the sources don't say
  (Q-20). Whether the SMK-37 has the FM-1's chip, the allowed sources don't
  say either: the emulator runs the SMK-37's own firmware on the FM-1's
  chip with a different panel, which is the emulator's view only.
- Sources: MAN (the SMK-37 Pro's manual, English part p. 3, "MIDI OUT":
  a 3.5 mm to MIDI adapter to an external device's MIDI In; Chinese part
  p. 15, USB MIDI, class-compliant; p. 16, Bluetooth; p. 17, the rear
  panel's MIDI output port); the MIDI 1.0 specification (the wire format);
  the emulator model (the SMK-37 board).
- Standing: confirmed (MAN)
- Needed by: M6b (MIDI out)

### HW-73: The UARTs' transmit side, and UART1's on the FM-1
- **Q-20. MIDI output on the chip.** Which UART and pin drive the
  SMK-37's MIDI OUT jack, and its port set-up (fixed pin pair or an output
  channel of `JL_IOMAP`; drive); how its TRS socket is wired (type A or B);
  whether the SMK-37 has the FM-1's chip; whether the FM-1's board brings
  UART1's transmit pin anywhere; which `CON0` bit enables the transmit
  interrupt; whether, after a DMA, the pending means the transfer has been
  read from RAM or the last stop bit has left the pin; whether the
  transmit DMA needs a 4-byte aligned address or length; what writing
  `TXCNT` does while a transfer is still going; how `BUF` and the DMA mix.
  Settled by a datasheet or a probe on real hardware (an SMK-37 and an
  FM-1).

  Settled by a datasheet or a probe on real hardware (an SMK-37 and an

    48 MHz clock and 191 from 24 MHz, both exact.

    pending; bits 6, 5 and 3 set together to receive by DMA.

content.text:
All five items are done. Four PRs are open and CI passes on three; #93's check was still running when I finished.

**1. fwtest 0.5.0 pin (#91).** The image published from #84's merge is pinned (`d4701f03…`) and reports fwtest 0.5.0. The firmware suite (main at `7b5144b`) passes on both 0.4.0 and 0.5.0. The results differ only in the version each one records and the new `midi_out_bytes_dropped` field, which is 0 in all 35 cases. The MIDI-out test image matches its golden files. M6b can start once #91 merges.

**2. Audit.** On main after #85 the self-test finds 30 of our 30 files. After #83 and #87 it finds 32 of 32, because MIDI in added two files. All three runs passed.

**3. The 0008 test fix (#92).** I applied the app's fix to our 0008 unchanged.
- Our old test's JIT half never ran compiled code (0 compiled entries).
- With the write counting switched off, the fixed test fails, and so does its JIT half on its own.
- All the emulator's own tests and the harness tests pass.
- I ran it only on this Mac (arm64), not on x86-64: CI runs the harness tests, not the emulator's.
- Only the test changed, so there's no new image to pin. The image workflow will still publish one when #92 merges; ignore it.
- The file that tracks the emulator's patches had an out-of-date hash and never listed the MIDI-out patch; both are fixed.
- In the records I described the fix as "taken unchanged, like the app's earlier patches". Please confirm the same MIT terms apply to it.

**4. Q-12 from another JieLi SDK (#93).**
- **Source:** `Jieli-Tech/fw-AC63_BT_SDK` at commit `fdc018de`. Its licence is the plain Apache-2.0 text with nothing added. Three of its chips have exactly our chip's UART registers at the same addresses.
- **Marking:** every fact from it is in a new entry, HW-75, with a new standing, "other chip (SDK63)". The spec checker accepts that standing only when the new SDK is cited, and its new test fails without the change.
- **What it answers, for those chips:**
  - the baud-rate formula: 383 gives 31,250 baud from 48 MHz;
  - 9-bit frames;
  - receiving without the DMA by polling;
  - the end of the receive buffer;
  - the second control register as flow control.
- **Where the chips disagree with ours:**
  - those chips code the UART clock choice differently from our chip;
  - they count the receive timeout in a different clock from fwtest's 48 MHz.

  fwtest is unchanged.
- **Still open (Q-12, Q-20):** a receive interrupt per byte without the DMA; error flags (none is used); what happens when the receive buffer overflows; the MIDI jack's pin; the TRS type.

**5. SMK-37 Pro manual.** There was no PDF in `drop/`, so HW-72's ManualsLib page numbers are unchecked. HW-72 now cites the Manuals+ write-up you supplied as a secondary source, with the pages you gave. Its "input/output" wording is recorded as unresolved, not as evidence of an input jack, and Q-20 stays open.

**Docker.** I removed this project's leftovers: 18 old fwtest and build tags and 3 old pulls of the published image. I kept both 0.4.0 (main still uses it until #91 merges) and 0.5.0, the current build image (the clean side was using it), `debian:bookworm-slim` and `eclipse-temurin:25-jre`. That freed only about 0.4 GB inside Docker, because most layers were shared. The Mac's free space is still 4.8 GB, since Docker Desktop doesn't hand space back to macOS on its own.
